subject: general
question: Purvanchal Himalayas does NOT comprise of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pir Panjal range**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Pir Panjal range**

 
• The Pir Panjal Range is situated in the Kashmir region.
 
• It is named after the Pir Panjal Pass.
 
• Indrasan is the highest peak of Pir Panjal Range.
 
 
• Mount Indrasan is located at an altitude of 6221 meters above sea level.
 
• It is one of the most difficult mountains to climb.
 
 
 
• Deo Tibba and Indrasan are the major peaks of Pir Panjal range.
 
• The Kashmir valley lies between the Himadri and Pir Panchal range.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Purvanchal Range, or Eastern Mountains, is a sub-mountain range of the Himalayas in North-East India.
 
• The Purvanchal comprises :
 
 
• The Patkai Hills
 
• The Naga Hills
 
• Manipur Hills
 
• The Mizo Hills
 
 
 
• The Patkai Hills:
 
 
• The Patkai Hills are the hills on India's north-eastern border with Burma or Myanmar.
 
 
 
• The Naga Hills:
 
 
• The Naga Hills lie on the border of India and Burma.
 
 
 
• The Mizo Hills:
 
 
• Mizo Hills is a mountain range in southeastern Mizoram state.
 
• Mizo Hills form part of the north Arakan Yoma system.
 
 
 
• The range is an eastern extension of the Himalayan Range System, in northeastern India.
 
• It bends sharply to the south beyond the Dihang River gorge and spreads along the eastern boundary of India with Myanmar. 
 
• The Purvanchal includes the hill of the Patkai hills, Naga Hills, Mizo Hills, and Manipur hills.
